We got three templates. Need to find which corresponds to carbonyl-ene. Look at first template: retro_smarts_template includes C-[Si] etc, not relevant. Second template: seems complex with aromatic etc. Third template: retro_smarts_template: '[C:1]-[CH2;D2;+0:2]-[C@H;D3;+0:3](-[C:4])-[C:5]=[C:6]>>[C:1]-[CH;D2;+0:2]=[C;H0;D3;+0:3](-[C:4])-[C:5]=[C:6]'. This looks like breaking a C-C single bond to form a C=C (i.e., converting a saturated carbon to alkene). That's like a retro-ene? The forward reaction would be C-C single bond + C=C to form C-C single and C=O? Not exactly.

But carbonyl-ene involves a carbonyl and alkene forming new C-C and C-O. The third template seems to involve a carbonyl? No O. So maybe not.

First template: retro_smarts_template: '[C:5]-[C@;H0;D4;+0:6](-[C:7])(-[OH;D1;+0:8])-[C;H0;D4;+0:1](-[F;D1;H0:2])(-[F;D1;H0:3])-[F;D1;H0:4]>>C-[Si](-C)(-C)-[C;H0;D4;+0:1](-[F;D1;H0:2])(-[F;D1;H0:3])-[F;D1;H0:4].[C:5]-[C;H0;D3;+0:6](-[C:7])=[O;H0;D1;+0:8]'

This seems to be a retro-aldol? It breaks a C-O bond? It shows product side with Si group (protecting). Not carbonyl-ene.

Second template: very complex, includes C-C(=O)-c1... and a large polycyclic. Might be carbonyl-ene? The retro_smarts_template: '[c:2]1:[cH;D2;+0:1]:[cH;D2;+0:4]:[c:5]:[cH;D2;+0:6]:[cH;D2;+0:3]:1>>C-C(=O)-c1:c:[cH;D2;+0:1]:[c:2]:[cH;D2;+0:3]:c:1.C-[C@]12-C-[C@H](-c3:c:[cH;D2;+0:4]:[c:5]:[cH;D2;+0:6]:c:3)-C3=C4-C-C-C5(-C=C-4-C-C-[C@@H]-3-[C@H]-1-C-C-C-2=O)-O-C-C-O-5'

That's huge, seems not.

Maybe the correct template is the third one, which is a simple retro-ene (C-C single to C=C). The forward reaction would be an ene reaction: an alkene and a carbonyl combine to give a new C-C bond and a C-O bond, converting C=O to OH and C=C to C-C. The retro would break C-O to C=O and C-C to C=C. The third template shows breaking a C-C single bond adjacent to a carbonyl? Actually it shows [C:5]=[C:6] unchanged, and [C:1]-[CH2]-[C@H](-[C:4])-[C:5]=[C:6] -> [C:1]-[CH]=[C](-[C:4])-[C:5]=[C:6]. That is converting a saturated carbon to alkene, not carbonyl.

But maybe the carbonyl is implicit elsewhere.

Given limited options, we need to return mapped_rxn and template_id. Which template likely matches our molecule? Our molecule contains a fluorinated carbon attached to a ring, plus OH. The third template's mapped_rxn includes many atoms with fluorine? Let's inspect mapped_rxn of third: '[CH2:1]=[CH:2][C:3]([F:4])([F:5])[C@:6]1([OH:7])...' This looks similar to our target: we have CH2= C with fluorines and OH. Indeed our target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]... )... plus fluorines at carbon 15 etc. The third template's mapped_rxn product side matches our product: CH2=CH? Actually product side: [CH2:1]=[CH:2][C:3]([F:4])([F:5])[C@:6]1([OH:7])... This matches a fluorinated carbon with OH in a ring. So third template seems to be the correct one.

Thus we should return its mapped_rxn and template_id (reaction_id? The field is reaction_id). The template_id is not given directly, but we have reaction_id and template_hash. The required output: template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). Likely the reaction_id is the template ID? In other tasks, template_id corresponds to reaction_id. We'll use reaction_id.

So for third entry: reaction_id = 6289, mapped_rxn = the long string. Let's extract mapped_rxn exactly from result.

From third entry: 'mapped_rxn': '[CH2:1]=[CH:2][C:3]([F:4])([F:5])[C@:6]1([OH:7])[CH2:8][CH2:9][C@H:10]2[C@@H:11]3[CH2:12][CH2:13][C:14]4=[CH:15][C:16](=[O:17])[CH2:18][CH2:19][C:20]4=[C:21]3[C@@H:22]([C:23]3=[CH:24]C=C(C(C)=O)C=[CH:29]3)[CH2:30][C@:31]12[CH3:32].CC=C(F)F.C[C@]12C[C@H](C3=C[CH:25]=[C:26]([Br:27])[CH:28]=C3)C3=C4CCC5(C=C4CC[C@H]3[C@@H]1CCC2=O)OCCO5>>[CH2:1]=[CH:2][C:3]([F:4])([F:5])[C@:6]1([OH:7])[CH2:8][CH2:9][C@H:10]2[C@@H:11]3[CH2:12][CH2:13][C:14]4=[CH:15][C:16](=[O:17])[CH2:18][CH2:19][C:20]4=[C:21]3[C@@H:22]([c:23]3[cH:24][cH:25][c:26]([Br:27])[cH:28][cH:29]3)[CH2:30][C@:31]12[CH3:32]'
